title: STAR-PólyaMath: Multi-Agent Reasoning under Persistent Meta-Strategic Supervision
claim: A supervised multi-agent system advances through staged loops with verification, trace-back and re-planning, bounding error propagation under persistent high-level oversight.
layout: Single wide flowchart, left-to-right, top supervisory banner with dashed intervention arrows, nested loop
description: A wide flowchart for a four-phase math-solving system. A large orange banner across the top, labeled Persistent Meta-Strategist, sends dashed orange arrows down into the stages (pre-plan analysis, exploration review, guides/directives). On the left, a Math Problem node leads through Explore (Reasoner) and Plan & Decompose (Reasoner), both in blue. The center is a gray box, Step Execution. Inside it, a dotted Challenge Loop shows a blue Reasoner and a yellow Verifier joined by circular arrows labeled Propose/Defend and Review/Challenge. Green arrows mark Accept and Solved paths. Yellow dashed arrows mark Trace-back and Propose Re-plan. On the right, a green Generate Solution box leads to Final Solution. A bottom hexagon, Replan Decision, leads to Failed and Partial Solution Saved or loops back with re-explore and re-plan. A legend and four phase labels sit along the bottom.
caption: STAR-PólyaMath system workflow. STAR-PólyaMath advances each problem with four phases: exploration, planning and decomposition, step-wise execution with challenge loops, and solution generation. A Python orchestrator dispatches the LLM agents and decides advance, trace-back, re-plan, and abort transitions. The Reasoner probes the problem, proposes a step-wise plan, and executes each step with hierarchical verification tags ([verified] / [easy-verify] / [hard-verify]). The Verifier reviews via logic and goal gates, and emits Accept, Challenge, Trace-Back, or Propose-Replan; persistent Reasoner-Verifier debate resolves disagreements within a step, while trace-back and re-planning bound error propagation across steps. A persistent Meta-Strategist supervises the trajectory with cross-attempt memory, issuing pre-planning analysis, strategic guidance or mandatory directives on timeout or stalemate, and re-plan verdicts.
abstract: Frontier AI models and multi-agent systems have led to significant improvements in mathematical reasoning. However, for problems requiring extended, long-horizon reasoning, existing systems continue to suffer from fundamental reliability issues: hallucination accumulation, memory fragmentation, and imbalanced reasoning-tool trade-offs. In this paper, we introduce STAR-PÃ³lyaMath, a multi-agent framework that systematically addresses these challenges through meta-level supervision and structured Reasoner-Verifier interaction. STAR-PÃ³lyaMath is structured as an orchestrated state machine with nested challenge-step-replan loops, governed by a reasoning-free Python orchestrator that separates control from inference and bounds error propagation through trace-back and re-planning. Our key innovation is a persistent Meta-Strategist that maintains cross-attempt memory and exercises meta-level control by issuing high-level strategic guidance or mandatory directives, so the system can escape unproductive loops rather than stagnate or over-rely on tools. STAR-PÃ³lyaMath achieves state-of-the-art results on all eight top-tier competition benchmarks: AIME 2025-2026, MathArena Apex Shortlist, MathArena Apex 2025, Putnam 2025, IMO 2025, HMMT February 2026, and USAMO 2026. It obtains perfect scores on AIMEs, Putnam, and HMMT, and shows its largest margin on Apex 2025, scoring 93.75% compared with 80.21% by the strongest baseline GPT-5.5. Ablation studies show that the gains arise from the framework's orchestration rather than from model-level diversity since removing key components or substituting in mixed backbones consistently weakens performance. Code is available at https://github.com/Julius-Woo/STAR-PolyaMath.
